title: Franceville students march against higher transport fares
location: Franceville, Haut-Ogooué; students marched toward Carrefour Potos. Exact route and other assembly points are not reported.
scope: Local city march by secondary-school students. Reports do not establish separate gatherings or turnout at individual schools or route points.
organizer: Students from several Franceville secondary schools; no formal organizing body is identified in the reviewed reports.
participants_original: Gabon Media Time reports hundreds of lycée and collège students; Info241 gives no attendance estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: GAB202301-S001 explicitly describes hundreds of students in the Franceville march, qualitatively exceeding 50. Exact attendance and counts at any individual school or site are not reported; no numeric bounds or separate gatherings are inferred.

title.summary: Both reports identify a Franceville student march against higher transport costs on 9 January 2023.

start_date.summary: The reports place the physical march in Franceville on Monday 9 January 2023; the publication date is also that day.

end_date.summary: None of the reviewed accounts establishes when participants stopped marching or dispersed. The reported class suspension through 14 January and planned 16 January reopening are administrative school dates, not physical assembly endpoints.

location.summary: The reports locate the march in Franceville; GAB202301-S001 describes a route toward Carrefour Potos. Exact start, route and end points remain incomplete.

scope.summary: Reports describe one Franceville city march by students from several schools. The school names and route do not establish separate attendance counts or distinct qualifying assemblies.

organizer.summary: Students from several schools are identified as marchers; no organizing group is named.

demands.summary: GAB202301-S001 reports a call for public-authority intervention over sharply increased transport costs and difficulty reaching class. GAB202301-S020 independently reports a fare protest and attributes a rise from FCFA 300 to 1,500 to some students; that fare figure is not a crowd count.

participants_original.summary: GAB202301-S001 describes hundreds of lycée and collège students. GAB202301-S020 supplies no turnout estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is encoded from the qualitative word hundreds.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The report's citywide description of hundreds qualitatively supports at least 50 participants; it does not support separate school/site counts or precise bounds.

protester_violence.summary: No reviewed article establishes event-specific protester violence. A report's concern about possible escalation is hypothetical; violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Both articles report a province-wide class suspension following the march, with reopening planned for 16 January. This administrative action does not establish physical dispersal or that the fare grievance was accommodated; other event-specific response dimensions are not reported.

eligibility.summary: GAB202301-S001 reports a physical city march, a qualitatively hundreds-sized crowd, and a request for public-authority intervention over fare increases. GAB202301-S020 separately reports the march but does not independently confirm turnout. This is a proposed local inclusion pending coordinator review.

notes: GAB202301-S001 and GAB202301-S002 are by the same author and outlet; S002 is not independent confirmation. GAB202301-S020 is a different outlet and story, corroborating the date, place and fare grievance, but it reports no turnout. Keep the event as one city march, not separate school or intersection events. The class suspension and planned reopening are not coded as the physical end, crowd dispersal or proven fare relief.
open_questions: What was the march's exact route, starting point and physical endpoint?
Does contemporaneous evidence identify distinct assembly sites, or only one city march? Do not create school-level events or counts without it.
Can an independent account corroborate the qualitative crowd description? No exact count or numeric bounds are presently available.
Did the provincial class suspension include an action that directly addressed the transport-fare grievance, beyond closing schools?
What event-specific state response, if any, occurred beyond the reported administrative class suspension?

title: Port-Gentil CNSS employees report joining a broader strike
location: CNSS premises in Port-Gentil; the report names the main gate and central courtyard but no street address.
scope: Potential local workplace picket or protest action. The report places it within a broader CNSS work stoppage in several cities, but does not establish the Port-Gentil episode's ownership or continuity.
organizer: Port-Gentil CNSS employees; no formal local organizer is named in the reviewed article.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The article describes a gate closure, tents, chairs and banners but gives no number of people assembled at the site. Staff totals or participation in the wider strike cannot substitute for a local simultaneous headcount.

title.summary: The article reports Port-Gentil CNSS employees joining a broader stoppage and describes physical action at the premises.

start_date.summary: The article does not give the date when the Port-Gentil physical action began. Its 12 January publication date is not substituted for event occurrence.

end_date.summary: No physical end, withdrawal from the gate or resumption date is reported. The article calls the broader strike indefinite.

location.summary: The report places Port-Gentil employees at CNSS's central gate and courtyard; it provides no exact address.

scope.summary: Only the reported Port-Gentil site is considered here. The article mentions employees in other cities, but does not show whether their actions were one coordinated national event or separate sites.

organizer.summary: The article identifies CNSS employees but no local union or organizing body.

demands.summary: The article attributes the action to alleged nonpayment or removal of salary benefits, including a thirteenth-month payment and fuel premium, and reports banners against provisional administrator Christophe Eyi.

participants_original.summary: No local attendance figure is reported.

participants_min.summary: No explicit numerical lower bound is reported; no numeric value is inferred from workforce or multi-city participation.

participants_max.summary: No local attendance maximum is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The described physical staging does not establish 50 simultaneous attendees at one public site; local turnout and public access are unreported.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not report event-specific protester violence; this remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The reviewed article does not establish an event-specific state response, dispersal, arrests, violence or accommodation.

eligibility.summary: The account reports physical staging at a workplace and a labor dispute, but actual start date, public-assembly status, one-site turnout, month ownership and a qualifying state-directed target remain unresolved.

notes: Gabonactu reports that Port-Gentil CNSS employees joined colleagues' wider strike, closed the central gate, set tents and chairs in the courtyard, and displayed banners. The report describes earlier strike phases and a possible resumption if commitments were unmet. This record does not treat the publication date as event onset, establish a continuous picket, borrow a national headcount, or merge the Port-Gentil site with actions elsewhere.
open_questions: When did the Port-Gentil physical action actually begin, and did it begin within January 2023?
How many people were simultaneously assembled at this site, and was the courtyard or gate action public and open?
Does the CNSS administrator or institution constitute a qualifying domestic state target for this labor demand, or is the action an employer dispute outside the target definition?
Is the Port-Gentil site action a new episode, a restart after a prior suspension, or a continuation of a CNSS strike that began before January?
When did the physical gate/courtyard action end, if it ended?
What event-specific state response or protester violence occurred, if any?
Does the blocked Info241 S006 article concern the same written story or an independent report? Its body was not read and its exact URL is stopped.
